pr_title: streamingest: fix returned cutover time on `complete to latest`
pr_body:
Currently when cutting over to the LATEST high watermark, the sql command prints that that cutover was done to timestamp 0.

This commit fixes this bug.

Fixes: #95901

Epic: CRDB-18752

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/96374)

merging, but if you think I should change anything I can do that in a followup, TFTR!
bors r+

issue_context.title: c2c: cutover to latest prints timestamp 0
issue_context.body:
```
root@localhost:26257/defaultdb> alter tenant dest1 complete replication to latest;
  cutover_time
----------------
         0E-10
(1 row)

Time: 48ms total (execution 48ms / network 0ms)
```
need to print the right time.. oops.

Jira issue: CRDB-23800

Epic CRDB-18752

review_comments: I do wonder if these tests could be data-driven tests.  But they are already written, so I leave that to your judgement.

good question.. I think I like the data driven tests for running through a user story such as setting up clusters and writing some things and doing a cutover etc., but here these 2 tests are the minimum code needed to verify one small thing which I think is useful. we can also do that with data driven but isn't it a bit harder to debug data driven tests? anyway, my point is that we need both but I see golang tests as better for unit tests and data driven better for longer story tests.
that said, I'll definitely try to remind myself to use data driven more..
